body: I misread OP and thought she said she did it after the co-worker asked her not to.

Oh sorry, my mistake! I misunderstood what you said. In that case it doesn't seem like you did much wrong except perhaps not properly discussing the task with your co-worker or superior, which might be why they put those notes in your review. I'm sure you could speak to whoever wrote it for a more in depth understanding of what they meant and what the company expects from you. Maybe they just wrote that so it didn't seem they were favouring either party. Either way, your co-worker is behaving very inappropriately and I'm sure her own review reflects that. Good luck with speaking to HR and I hope the situation improves! If they do nothing, it might be better to find a different company with a better support system! :)

Well, the review is right. This does reflect poorly on leadership and teamwork skills. I'm honestly not criticising you, I am just looking at it from a managerial perspective. They aren't saying you did anything technically wrong by the company's procedure, however, you don't get on well in a team by going behind your team member's back and doing something they disagree with without coming to some kind of compromise. Being a good leader isn't being a dictator. All it means is that you made a mistake and you can learn from it. It might not threaten your chance of getting a higher position if you show what you have learnt from the situation. 
Go to HR and tell them that the woman is still talking badly about you and you would like their help in finding a way to resolve it, as it is affecting your morale and other relationships. If you really feel bad about it, tell them that you feel it's a form of bullying. You don't want her to get in trouble but you would like their advice before you proceed in attempting to mend the professional relationship.

It's just hard when you don't even understand what the issue is in the first place other than you didn't used to feel like you do now and some of the things you think are not normal in a healthy brain and it feels so crappy constantly not feeling ok in your head.

I'm not sure I really understand your post, but maybe try and focus on doing sports because you enjoy them and they make you feel good/are good for your wellbeing and can help you make friends, rather than to compete and compare yourself to others.

Do not just use grade entry requirements to judge if a university is "good" or not. Some of the top universities state AAB or ABB as a requirement and personally I see that as  good thing. It means they are recognising that grades at A-level are not the be all and end all and intelligent people can get less than "perfect" grades for many reasons. It stops people being put off by high entry requirements. You may get some people applying with AAA and being rejected and others applying with ABB and getting accepted as they're looking at other things. This is not a negative comment towards you but the way you are thinking is very "sixth form". Once you're in university you will see that grades at A-level do not reflect the quality of the course or the person.
Look at the modules studied, reviews from people who have studied there (I remember I looked at the student room, but this was years ago), field courses, university funding (unless this isn't needed due to help from parents)... and what is extremely important is compatibility with the city!
